i1.title: AI-native engineering

process.title: From business problem to a system that keeps improving
process.sub: Six steps we use on client projects and on our own products. In each one, AI speeds up the work and engineers make the decisions.

s1.title: Discover
s1.text: Understand the business goal, the users and how the work is done today.
s1.ai: Summarising existing documents and drafting question lists for you to confirm.

s2.title: Understand the systems
s2.text: Map existing systems, data, constraints and integration points.
s2.ai: Reading existing code and specifications to speed up analysis.

s3.title: Design
s3.text: Agree on architecture, scope and the right level of AI, which is sometimes none.
s3.ai: Exploring design alternatives and drafting specifications for review.

s4.title: Build
s4.text: Deliver in small, reviewable increments with regular demos.
s4.ai: Code generation and review assistance, always checked by an engineer.

s5.title: Validate
s5.text: Test functionality, security basics and, for AI features, answer quality.
s5.ai: Generating test cases and test data; evaluating AI outputs against test questions.

s6.title: Operate and improve
s6.text: Release, monitor and keep improving with you after launch.

bis2.heroTitle: BIS: turning Biology knowledge into intelligence that scales
bis2.heroText: BIS is an AI-native system that structures Biology knowledge so that AI can teach it, check understanding, and improve with every learner and every teacher review.
bis2.problemTitle: Knowledge exists. Intelligence does not scale.
bis2.problemText: Most Biology learning still arrives as videos, slides, PDFs and one-way lectures. A student who misunderstands a concept is rarely detected, and a teacher cannot personalise explanations for every learner.
bis2.solutionTitle: A knowledge system, not just more content
bis2.solutionText: BIS models Biology as concepts, relations, evidence and common misconceptions. On top of this structure, AI can explain with citations, practise with the right questions, and track what each learner has mastered.

f1.title: Structured knowledge
f1.text: Concepts, relations, evidence and misconceptions are modelled explicitly, versioned and traceable.

f2.title: AI tutor with citations
f2.text: Answers are grounded in approved source passages and show where they come from.

f3.title: Adaptive practice
f3.text: Questions are linked to concepts and misconceptions, so wrong answers reveal why a learner is stuck.

f4.title: Mastery tracking
f4.text: The system keeps a mastery state per concept to guide what to practise next.

f5.title: Teacher in the loop
f5.text: AI drafts questions and content as drafts. A Biology teacher reviews and approves before anything is served.

f6.title: Trustworthy by design
f6.text: Every change is traceable, content comes only from self-written or openly licensed sources.

bis2.todayText: The current prototype includes a student portal with practice questions, a source-cited AI tutor, mastery tracking and an admin review workflow. Content is still draft and is being prepared for review by Biology teachers.

road1.title: Now
road1.text: Working prototype, first Biology scope: cell biology, molecular biology and genetics.

road2.title: Next
road2.text: Teacher-reviewed content, real user accounts, and a pilot with advanced high-school Biology and competition preparation.

road3.title: Later
road3.text: More subjects and levels, such as university and vocational education. This is a direction, not a delivered scope.

q1.title: Who is BIS for?
q1.text: Our first focus is advanced high-school Biology in Vietnam, including competition preparation. Teachers, schools and learning programmes are our target audience.

q2.title: Is BIS available now?
q2.text: BIS is an experimental prototype. If you are a teacher or school interested in a pilot or in giving feedback, please email us.

q3.title: How do you keep AI answers accurate?
q3.text: The tutor answers from approved source passages and shows citations. AI-written questions stay as drafts until a Biology teacher approves them.

q4.title: Where does the content come from?
q4.text: We use content we write ourselves or sources with open licences. Copyrighted textbooks are not used without permission.

bis2.ctaText: Teachers, schools and partners are welcome to ask about a pilot or share feedback.

k3.title: BPMN workflow
k3.text: Modelling business processes in BPMN and running them on a workflow engine such as Camunda, with AI agents and Microsoft 365 connected in, so approvals, tasks and integrations are explicit, automated and measurable.

aab.text: Business process automation that combines BPMN workflows on Camunda, AI agents and Microsoft 365.

aab.heroTitle: AAB: automate business processes with BPMN and AI agents
aab.heroText: AAB models a business process in BPMN, runs it on Camunda, lets AI agents handle the steps that need reading and judgement, and brings people in through Microsoft 365.
aab.problemTitle: Processes live in inboxes and spreadsheets
aab.problemText: Many business processes still run through email, files and memory. Approvals stall, documents are retyped, and nobody can see where a case is stuck or why.
aab.solutionTitle: Make the process explicit, then automate it
aab.solutionText: AAB turns a process into a BPMN model and executes it. AI agents take on steps that used to need a person to read, classify or draft, while people stay in control of decisions.

c1.title: BPMN workflow on Camunda
c1.text: Each process runs step by step on a workflow engine, with state, timers, approvals and a full history.

c2.title: AI agents
c2.text: Agents classify requests, extract data from documents and draft replies, using your knowledge and tools.

c3.title: Microsoft 365
c3.text: Requests, approvals and notifications reach people where they already work, through Microsoft 365.

c4.title: Human in control
c4.text: AI proposes, people decide. Sensitive steps stay under human approval, and every action is traceable.

aab.whereText: AAB is in development. We are building the BPMN workflow core on Camunda, drawing on our experience delivering BPMN and workflow projects for Japanese clients.

q1.title: What does AAB do?
q1.text: It automates business processes: modelled in BPMN, executed on a workflow engine, with AI agents for the steps that need reading, classifying or drafting.

q2.title: Is AAB available now?
q2.text: AAB is in development. If you have a process you would like to automate, email us to talk about it.

q3.title: Does AI replace people?
q3.text: No. AI handles preparation work, people approve and decide, and the system records what happened.

founderMsg.title: Building an AI-native engineering company
founderMsg.quote: Technology creates its greatest value when the engineers building it understand the business problem behind it.
founderMsg.p1: I trained in the HEDSPI programme at Hanoi University of Science and Technology, a Vietnam–Japan IT engineering programme supported by JICA. Alongside the technical curriculum, we studied the Japanese language and Japanese working culture in depth. After graduating, I began working on software for Japanese clients in 2011, and over the following years moved from writing code to leading projects and delivery, across ERP, embedded systems, business workflow, healthcare and AI. One lesson kept repeating: technology creates its greatest value when the engineers building it understand the business problem behind it.
founderMsg.p2: Too often, outsourcing turns engineers into ticket-takers. The specification arrives, the code is delivered, and nobody asks whether it solves the real problem. That model breaks down when a customer's challenge is unclear, spans several systems, or changes as the work progresses.
founderMsg.p3: I founded Brisasoft in 2024 because AI is changing how software is designed, built and operated, and engineering teams must change with it. We use AI throughout our work so that engineers can spend more of their time on what matters: understanding the context, challenging assumptions and exploring better solutions.
founderMsg.p4: Our ambition is for every Brisasoft engineer to develop a Forward Deployed Engineer mindset: technical depth, business understanding, practical problem-solving and close collaboration with customers. We are building that capability step by step, and it is the standard we hold ourselves to.
founderMsg.p5: AI helps us work more effectively, but it does not replace engineering judgement, responsibility, or the trust built between people. We value professionalism, dedication, transparency and continuous improvement, and we will tell you plainly when a simpler or non-AI solution is the better choice.
founderMsg.p6: We want to be more than a software vendor: a dependable technology partner that helps you turn business challenges into practical, sustainable solutions. Thank you for considering Brisasoft.

quality.title: How we keep delivery predictable
quality.sub: Practices we apply on every engagement, scaled to the size of the project.

q1.title: Requirements clarification
q1.text: Open questions are tracked in a shared Q&A list until each one is answered.

q2.title: Technical design
q2.text: Architecture and specification documents are reviewed before development starts.

q3.title: Code review
q3.text: Every change is reviewed by another engineer. AI-assisted review is an extra check, not a replacement.

q4.title: Testing
q4.text: Unit, integration and acceptance testing, with test cases traceable to requirements.

q5.title: Security checks
q5.text: Dependency checks, no secrets in source code, and access limited to what each environment needs.

q6.title: Documentation
q6.text: Specifications, operating notes and decisions kept up to date as the system changes.

q7.title: Progress reporting
q7.text: Regular reports on progress, risks and open issues, in a format agreed with you.

q8.title: Knowledge transfer
q8.text: Handover material and sessions so your team can operate and extend the system.

team.title: Our team
team.text: Our engineers graduated from leading Vietnamese universities for IT, including Hanoi University of Science and Technology and Hanoi University of Industry. 70% of our engineers are AI engineers who also develop back end and front end, and every engineer uses AI tools in daily work.
